title: Enterprise ask portfolios and minimum viable scope
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Purpose: create a lightweight, repeatable process for consolidating multiple enterprise feature asks from Sales and Customer Success into portfolio-level opportunities with a recommended minimum viable scope (MVS) for initial scoping. Background: Sales/CS frequently submit related asks across accounts (authz/RBAC variants, enhanced audit logging, region-specific deployment controls). Engineers and PMs spend ad-hoc time re-evaluating similar asks instead of operating off a consolidated portfolio and an agreed MVS. Goal: reduce time-to-first-scope by providing a 15-30 minute triage artifact per portfolio that captures representative customers, value hypothesis, rough effort band, proposed MVS (one-sprint slice), and suggested next-step (pilot, research spike, or backlog grooming). Out of scope: deep technical design, implementation plans, or multi-quarter roadmaps. Success metrics: reduce initial scoping latency from average 7 business days to <=2 business days; increase alignment between Sales/CS and PMs on acceptance criteria for early pilots.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable template (Confluence page) exists to capture portfolio summary, representative accounts, value hypothesis, MVS, effort band, and recommended next step
Pilot-ready MVS created for the top 3 incoming portfolios with linked sample tickets and a single canonical demo flow
Triage cycle time metric instrumented on the intake board (time from ask submission to MVS publish) and dashboarded
Stakeholders from Sales, CS, and Solutions Eng have reviewed and signed off on MVS for at least two pilot portfolios
decisions: Use 'portfolio' as the primary aggregation unit rather than product area to reflect cross-account feature alignment
Adopt a single-page MVS template to ensure scoping fits a single sprint-equivalent effort (<=5 points) for initial pilot
Triage cadence: weekly intake review with rotating PM owner; urgent asks can trigger ad-hoc review
tradeoffs: Keeping MVS deliberately small reduces scope risk but may split customer expectations across follow-up work
Consolidation adds initial cognitive overhead for Sales reps but improves long-term predictability for Eng
Prioritizing portfolio-level asks may deprioritize single-account quick wins—need explicit carve-out policy

2025-03-03: PM sync—agreed to run two one-week spikes (RBAC pilot + audit export spike) before full scoping. Cycle updated to 2025-W11. Assigned Aisha to coordinate pilots.
